description: I am Eshaan, I am keen on astrophysics, coding and AI/ML, along with gaming and simulations.
summary:
Most space games simplify survival down to basic health bars. Our challenge was building a simulator that feels genuinely realistic without turning into a dry spreadsheet or requiring a gaming supercomputer.

Everything had to run inside a standard web browser with zero backend. The biggest technical hurdle was getting very different simulation layers to talk to each other seamlessly—transitioning from orbital mechanics to a 9-stage hypersonic landing, into first-person base walking with real collision physics, and finally onto a rover-ready Martian surface.

On top of the 3D graphics, we had to model real NASA life-support math under the hood. Balancing oxygen, food, water recycling, and solar power during unpredictable dust storms meant every subsystem had to interact like a real habitat. Keeping players hooked across 30 days without repeating the same loop was tough, so we designed a daily return-to-base cycle where equipment wear, crew fatigue, and random emergencies force you to make tough survival calls every morning.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

JAMN is a client-side, browser-native Mars expedition simulator that takes users through a full mission lifecycle across four continuous segments:

  1. Interplanetary Flight Deck & Reconnaissance: First-person cockpit piloting, orbital insertion, and site evaluation using verified NASA/JPL Viking, MOLA, and MRO terrain data.
  2. EDL & Surface EVA: A telemetry-calibrated 9-stage hypersonic descent sequence followed by 0.38g0.38g0.38g low-gravity surface EVA and regolith sampling.
  3. 3D Habitat Operations & Diagnostics: Hyperbaric airlock cycle (0.62 to 101.3 kPa0.62\text{ to }101.3\text{ kPa}0.62 to 101.3 kPa), interactive first-person interior navigation, Gazebo ODE contact physics, and slide-in hardware repair terminals.
  4. 30-Sol Surface Survival Engine: A diurnal simulation clock running continuous differential equations for metabolic O2\text{O}_2O2​, caloric intake, closed-loop H2O\text{H}_2\text{O}H2​O recovery, and hybrid Kilopower fission/solar power generation, complemented by dynamic daily operational challenges.

What benefits does it have?

  • Scientific Rigor Over Simplification: Replaces arbitrary game health bars with real closed-loop environmental control and life-support systems (ECLSS) trade-offs.
  • Operational Systems Intuition: Demonstrates how daily human decisions—such as skipping physical exercise countermeasures or misallocating discretionary Crew-Hours (CH)—cascade into compounding conditioning debt, equipment degradation, and electrical blackouts.
  • Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Runs entirely in modern web browsers without external dependencies, expensive hardware, or complex installation hurdles.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To democratize human spaceflight training and aerospace systems engineering education for students, educators, and space enthusiasts globally. By transforming published NASA specifications into an engaging, interactive simulation, JAMN inspires the next generation of engineers and astronauts to solve real-world life-support, orbital, and planetary survival challenges.

How is your project creative?

  • Unified Multi-Paradigm Simulation: Bridges macro-scale orbital mechanics, intermediate hypersonic EDL, micro-scale interior habitat repairs, and open-world rocker-bogie rover exploration into a single cohesive story arc.
  • Dynamic Daily Deployment Loop: Eliminates repetitive gameplay across 30 sols by routing the astronaut through nightly base returns, tactical diagnostic sweeps, and randomized daily challenge scenarios.
  • Dual-Perspective Surface Traversal: Offers seamless switching between third-person articulated spacesuit locomotion, realistic helmet-visor HUD telemetry, and rover chase dynamics.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Empirical Scientific Grounding: Calibrated against NASA Baseline Values and Assumptions Document (BVAD Rev. 2) and CHAPEA 4-person metabolic metrics.
  • Planetary Environmental Accuracy: Topography, elevation, thermal swings, and atmospheric densities modeled strictly after authentic Martian landing sites (Valles Marineris, Planum Boreum, Olympus Mons, Hellas Basin).
  • Physical Dynamics & Constraint Modeling: Gazebo contact physics (0.38g0.38g0.38g, solid capsule colliders, non-phasing boundaries), realistic solar dust attenuation (τ\tauτ), and automatic 4-tier electrical load shedding cascades.
  • Inclusive Hardware Optimization: Integrated low-spec performance configurations to ensure smooth 60 FPS execution on budget academic laptops and classroom Chromebooks.
